blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-accessibility-1 (Delete action is a clickable div, unreachable with the keyboard) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-accessibility-2 (Icon-only delete control has no accessible name) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Render the delete action as a native `<button type="button">` (keeping the `icon-button` class) instead of a `<div>` with `onClick`. A keyboard user pressing Tab never lands on the div (no `tabindex`), and Enter or Space does nothing (no key handler), so a keyboard-only user cannot delete a document — the one task this change adds. A screen reader announces no role, so the action is not exposed as a control either. WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard, 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value. Once it is a button, check that the `.icon-button` style keeps a visible focus indicator (2.4.7).
findings.title: Delete action is a clickable div, unreachable with the keyboard

findings.recommendation: Give the control a text name, e.g. `aria-label="Delete document"` on the button (or visually hidden text), and mark the icon decorative (`aria-hidden="true"` on the SVG). The only content is `<TrashIcon />`, so a screen reader user reaching the control hears no name, or "button" alone, and cannot tell it deletes the document. WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content, 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value.
findings.title: Icon-only delete control has no accessible name

findings.recommendation: Add an `alt`: the owner's name (e.g. `alt={ownerName}`, passing the name as a prop) since the avatar identifies the document's owner, or `alt=""` if the owner's name is shown as text elsewhere. Without `alt`, screen readers announce the image URL or file name, which is noise and does not convey who owns the document. WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content.
findings.title: Owner avatar has no alt attribute
